title: MPSC Order — Case No. U-20604: Approves the application
text:
S T A T E O F M I C H I G A N 

BEFORE THE MICHIGAN PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 

* * * * * 

In the matter of the application of
) 
CONSUMERS ENERGY COMPANY 
) 
for approval of power purchase agreements.
)
Case No. U-20604 
) 

At the November 4, 2021 meeting of the Michigan Public Service Commission in Lansing, 
Michigan. 

PRESENT: Hon. Daniel C. Scripps, Chair 

Hon. Tremaine L. Phillips, Commissioner 

Hon. Katherine L. Peretick, Commissioner 

ORDER 

On October 8, 2021, Consumers Energy Company (Consumers) filed an application pursuant 
to Section 6j of Public Act 304 of 1982, MCL 460.6j requesting ex parte approval of a power 
purchase agreement (PPA) with Dow Silicones Corporation (DSC), for the output of the DSC 
Corp Center Solar Plant. 

In its application, Consumers recounts that on September 3, 2009, Consumers and Dow 
Corning Corporation (predecessor to DSC) entered into an Experimental Advanced Renewable 
Program (EARP) agreement for the output of the DSC Corp Center Solar Plant. The EARP 
agreement was approved as Contract Number 1 in the December 21, 2010 order in Case No. 
U-15805. Consumers’ application, pp. 1-2. Consumers explains that, as part of the EARP pilot 
under the company’s renewable energy plan, Contract Number 1 provided Consumers with 

Page 2 
U-20604 
energy, capacity, and renewable energy credits. The initial term of the EARP agreement ended 
September 3, 2021. 

In the instant application, Consumers states that it executed a new PPA on September 8, 2021, 
for the 31.3 kilowatt (kW) output of the DSC Corp Center Solar Plant. The term began on 
September 4, 2021, and ends on May 31, 2032. Id., p. 2; direct testimony of Beth Skowronski, 
p. 2. Per Consumers, the payments for the PPA are based on Consumers’ Public Utility 
Regulatory Policies Act of 1978, PL 95–617; 92 Stat 3117 (PURPA) full avoided cost rates as 
approved in the May 26, 2021 order in Case No. U-20165. The company further states that the 
PPA provides for the purchase of capacity from the plant based on zonal resource credits (ZRCs). 
The payment is made on a monthly basis at a fixed rate of $5,551.92 per ZRC-month. The 
purchase of energy is based on an escalating rate (dollar per megawatt-hour) as contained in 
Exhibit No. A-2 of the PPA attached to Consumers’ application. The PPA also includes a 
regulatory disallowance clause, a monthly administrative charge, and an early termination security 
provision. Additionally, Consumers notes that the PPA is subject to the financial compensation 
mechanism approved in Case No. U-20165. The PPA is also based on the company’s PURPA 
standard offer PPA, as filed on June 18, 2021 in Case No. U-20165. Consumers estimates that the 
savings to customers over the 10-year term of the PPA will be $156,000, when compared to the 
costs of the expired EARP agreement. Consumers’ application, pp. 2-3. 
Discussion 

MCL 460.6j(13) provides, in relevant part, that in a power supply cost reconciliation, the 
Commission shall do all of the following: 
(b) Not disallow the capacity charges for any facilities for which the electric utility 
would otherwise have a purchase obligation if the commission has approved 
capacity charges in a contract with a qualifying facility, as that term is defined by 

Page 3 
U-20604 
the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission pursuant to the public utilities 
regulatory policies act of 1978, Public Law 95-617, 92 Stat 3117, unless the 
commission has ordered revised capacity charges upon reconsideration under this 
subsection. A contract is valid and binding in accordance with its terms, and 
capacity charges paid pursuant to that contract are recoverable costs of the utility 
for rate-making purposes notwithstanding that the order approving that contract is 
later vacated, modified, or otherwise held to be invalid in whole or in part if the 
order approving the contract has not been stayed or suspended by a competent court 
within 30 days after the date of the order, or by July 29, 1987 if the order was 
issued after September 1, 1986 and before June 29, 1987. The commission shall 
determine the scope and manner of the review of capacity charges for a qualifying 
facility. Except as to approvals for qualifying facilities granted by the commission 
before June 1, 1987, proceedings before the commission seeking those approvals 
shall be conducted as a contested case pursuant to chapter 4 of the administrative 
procedures act of 1969, 1969 PA 306, MCL 24.271 to 24.287. The commission, 
upon its own motion or upon application of any person, may reconsider its approval 
of capacity charges for a qualifying facility in a contested case hearing after passage 
of a period necessary for financing the qualifying facility, if both of the following 
apply: 

(i) The commission has first issued an order making a finding based on evidence 
presented in a contested case that there has been a substantial change in 
circumstances since the commission’s initial approval. 

(ii) The commission finding is set forth in a commission order subject to immediate 
judicial review. 

The Commission has reviewed Consumers’ application, the supporting testimony and exhibits, 
and the language in MCL 460.6j, and finds that the PPA should be approved. The Commission 
further finds that ex parte review and approval are appropriate as approval will not affect rates or 
rate schedules and will not increase the cost of service to customers. See, MCL 460.6a(3). 

THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED that the power purchase agreement between Consumers 
Energy Company and Dow Silicones Corporation for the output of the DSC Corp Center Solar 
Plant is approved as in compliance with Public Act 304 of 1982. 

The Commission reserves jurisdiction and may issue further orders as necessary. 

Page 4 
U-20604 

Any party desiring to appeal this order must do so in the appropriate court within 30 days after 
issuance and notice of this order, pursuant to MCL 462.26. To comply with the Michigan Rules of 
Court’s requirement to notify the Commission of an appeal, appellants shall send required notices 
to both the Commission’s Executive Secretary and to the Commission’s Legal Counsel. 
Electronic notifications should be sent to the Executive Secretary at mpscedockets@michigan.gov 
and to the Michigan Department of the Attorney General - Public Service Division at 
pungp1@michigan.gov. In lieu of electronic submissions, paper copies of such notifications may 
be sent to the Executive Secretary and the Attorney General - Public Service Division at 7109 
W. Saginaw Hwy., Lansing, MI 48917.
